channel.title: Everyday Japan Studio — Articles
channel.description: Free explainers from Everyday Japan Studio — practical Japan topics checked against official Japanese sources.

item.title: How Japan's Tax-Free Refund System Works (Since November 2026)
item.description: Japan replaced tax-free-at-the-register with a refund system on 1 November 2026. Pay full price, confirm at Customs before you check your bags, then the store refunds the tax. The threshold, the 90-day deadline, the math, and the traps that cancel refunds.

item.title: Is the JR Pass Worth It in 2026? The Break-Even Math
item.description: Verified JR Pass prices, the break-even test based on travel days rather than trip days, the Nozomi supplement, and regional passes that often beat the national pass.

item.title: Onsen With Tattoos: House Rule, Not Law
item.description: No Japanese law bans tattoos in baths. What the Public Bath Act and the Tourism Agency's 2016 notice actually say, the three answers a facility can give, Kinosaki's confirmed yes, and how to check any bath before you go.

item.title: Goshugi: How Much Cash to Give at a Japanese Wedding
item.description: The ¥30,000 benchmark for a friend's wedding, customary amounts by relationship from the Zexy Wedding Trend Survey 2024, the number rules, new bills, and envelope basics.

item.title: Ho-Ren-So: The Reporting System Japanese Offices Run On
item.description: Report, inform, consult — three different acts that foreign staff keep merging into one. The spinach pun, the 1982 origin, and the timing rules nobody states out loud.

item.title: Otoshi: The Dish You Didn't Order at the Izakaya
item.description: Why a small dish arrives before you've ordered anything, what it costs (usually ¥200–¥1,000), whether you can refuse it, and the separate seat charge to ask about.
